profile.name: Meriem Trabelsi
profile.title: Software Development Engineer
profile.headline: I build cloud-native, event-driven systems where business processes are models, not buried code.
about: Engineer in software development from the Higher Institute of Computer Science (ISI), University of Tunis El Manar.

My focus is process automation and event-driven microservices. My graduation project at IT Serv orchestrates a telecom fibre order end to end with Kogito, Drools and Apache Kafka, aligned with the TM Forum Open APIs.

I also bring full-stack experience with Spring Boot and Angular, and applied deep learning for computer vision. I care about SOLID principles, design patterns and architecture decisions that are written down with their cost.

spotlight.title: TM Forum and BPMN, working together
spotlight.intro: A telecom order crosses systems that were never designed to cooperate. I make that journey explicit: TM Forum standards say what is exchanged, a BPMN model says in which order, and an engine runs it.

tmforum.text: The TM Forum publishes the frameworks and Open APIs that let operator systems interoperate without custom work. My graduation project follows them end to end.
tmforum.proof: Measured with the official TM Forum conformance kits: 4,362 of 5,403 assertions pass; 7 of 8 blocking issues fixed.
tmforum.cert: Certified: Introduction to the TM Forum and the Open Digital Architecture (ODA), TM Forum, May 2026

bpmn.text: The sequence of the journey is not written in Java. It is a BPMN 2.0 model, compiled by Kogito at build time and executed as it is drawn. Business decisions live beside it in Drools rules.

projects.name: O2A Service, Order-to-Activate Orchestration
projects.summary: A TM Forum-aligned platform that carries a fibre order from the eligibility check to the first invoice, driven by one executable BPMN model instead of hand-written glue.
highlights: One BPMN model of 118 nodes in five lanes, executed by Kogito 10.2
52 Drools rules, each file owned by the service that consults it
9 microservices, 8 PostgreSQL databases, 22 Kafka topics, 17 TM Forum Open APIs (v4)
Compensation in reverse order when a journey cannot succeed; technical failures stay resumable
Measured on the live stack: 54 end-to-end checks, 50 concurrent orders at a 0.10 s median
A port double-booking found under concurrency, fixed with a conditional database write
